$comment: Third-party false-green corpus rows (#130 item 1). A row's ground truth is SOMEBODY ELSE'S: an upstream commit that fixed a bug and shipped the regression test for it. The oracle is that test, run against the broken source. Refs are immutable, so upstream cannot move a row under the measurement. Candidates are found with find-candidate-rows.mjs; a candidate becomes a row ONLY after the fail/pass below is measured, because an unverified row makes the scorecard read stronger than it is.

rows.subject: Fix queue item double click

failing: goToIndex to the current index does not stop playback
goToId with the current item id does not stop playback
verified.note: Exactly the two tests the fix shipped fail, and the other 32 still pass. The oracle discriminates this defect specifically rather than reporting the build broken.

rows.whyItIsAFalseGreen: Double-clicking the queue item that is already playing silently STOPS playback. The item is selected, the queue renders correctly, and nothing on screen says anything is wrong — the failure is a state change nobody asked for. A presence-only check of the queue UI passes here, which is exactly the shape this corpus exists to measure.

boot.$comment: The renderer is a Vite app; `pnpm dev` is `tauri dev` and needs a Rust toolchain, but vite alone serves the same frontend as an ordinary web page. Measured: ready in 1.5s, HTTP 200.

drive.$comment: What Reticle must catch. The defect is a state change nobody asked for: activating the ALREADY-PLAYING queue item stops playback. Declared as the consequence an agent would asserting on it, so a miss here is a false green in the exact sense this corpus measures.
drive.defect: activating the already-current queue item stops playback
drive.note: Requires the app to reach a playing queue, which needs its own setup on this fixture. Not yet automated; see verify-rows.mjs --drive.
